heroHeadline: Pakistan Demands 'Decisive Action' Against TTP Camps on Day 80 — Five Suicide Attacks in Six Days Kill 30+ Security Forces
heroSubtitle: On May 16, 2026 (Day 80 of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq), Pakistan's defence and political establishment reached a 'decisive action' consensus following five TTP suicide attacks in six days (May 9–14) that killed at least 30 Pakistani security personnel across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's border districts. The attacks — Bannu (May 9), Fateh Khel VBIED (May 10, 15+ police), KPK (May 11, 15 policemen), Lakki Marwat (May 12), and Meena Scouts Camp Bajaur VBIED (May 14, 11–15 soldiers) — represent the most sustained TTP mass-casualty campaign of 2026, demonstrating that Pakistan's diplomatic non-escalation framework has not reduced TTP operational tempo. Pakistan COAS Field Marshal Asim Munir's warning that the fight against TTP facilitators will continue 'until its logical conclusion' stands as the operative military posture on Day 80. Pakistan's summoning of the Taliban deputy envoy on May 15 (Day 79) was followed by Al Jazeera's report that the Afghanistan ceasefire is 'at risk.' The Taliban IEA continues to categorically deny providing sanctuary to TTP. No formal ceasefire exists. No Urumqi Round 2 date has been announced. China remains publicly silent since its April 8 Foreign Ministry briefing. Three journalists — TOLO News presenters Mansoor Niazi and Imran Danish, and Paigard News Agency head Jawid Niazi — remain in Taliban custody; UN and Amnesty International have demanded their release.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNAMA, SIGAR, ACLED, Brown University Costs of War Project, US DoD, Reuters, BBC, Al Jazeera, Tolo News, Dawn, Geo News, HRW, OHCHR, OCHA
